prompt: You need sign-off from an analytical, detail-focused architect.
why: Send the full proposal with data and trade-offs in advance and allow time for questions.
trap: A two-line summary suits D, but C will want the detail.

prompt: A precise, rule-following teammate questions a new process.
why: Explain the logic and evidence, and how quality is protected.
trap: Reassurance about feelings suits S; C wants reasons.

prompt: You need to give feedback to a careful expert who hates being wrong.
tells: careful expert who hates being wrong
why: Be specific and factual, focus on the work, and give examples and time to respond.

prompt: Your proposal came back with a long list of numbered questions from a meticulous reviewer.
why: Answer each one precisely, in writing, with evidence.
trap: Calling to talk it through casually suits i; C wants written answers.

prompt: A meeting includes a reserved analyst who needs time to think before giving an opinion.
tells: needs time to think before giving an opinion
why: Send the agenda and materials in advance, then ask for their analysis.
trap: Springing a decision in the room suits D.

prompt: A quality-focused engineer won't commit to a date without understanding the requirements fully.
tells: won't commit to a date without understanding the requirements fully
why: Give clear, written requirements and the constraints, then ask for an estimate.
trap: Pushing for a gut-feel date suits D.

prompt: You're pitching a tool to a skeptical, data-driven finance lead.
why: Bring numbers, sources and a comparison of alternatives.

prompt: You're handing a task to a meticulous teammate who likes to do things right the first time.
tells: likes to do things right the first time
why: Give clear standards, examples and the definition of done.
trap: Just the goal and freedom suits D.

prompt: You found a mistake in a precise colleague's report, and they take quality very seriously.
why: Point to the specific error privately and factually, without judgment.
trap: Joking about it in a group suits nobody, least of all C.

prompt: Write to a colleague who replies to every vague email with 'Can you be more specific?'
why: Be precise: numbers, dates, links and exact asks.
trap: Warm and friendly without details won't help C.
